title: AWS Cloud Infrastructure Engineer

This role is responsible for establishing secure, scalable, highly available, and resilient AWS infrastructure across Development, Test, UAT, Parallel Run, and Production environments. The ideal candidate will possess extensive hands-on expertise in AWS cloud architecture, infrastructure automation, network design, security, disaster recovery, and environment provisioning. Experience supporting Micro Focus Enterprise Server or Rocket Enterprise Server workloads and large-scale application migration programs is highly desirable. This role will work closely with application modernization, database migration, DevOps, security, and platform engineering teams to ensure the cloud infrastructure is optimized to support mission-critical workloads throughout migration, testing, parallel validation, and production deployment phases. What you will do: Design and implement scalable AWS landing zones and cloud infrastructure architectures to support enterprise mainframe modernization programs. Architect and provision Development, Test, UAT, Parallel Run, Disaster Recovery, and Production environments. Define AWS infrastructure standards, security controls, governance policies, and operational best practices. Design secure networking architecture including: Amazon VPC Route 53 Security Groups Network ACLs NAT Gateways AWS Direct Connect VPN Connectivity Hybrid Cloud Networking Deploy and manage compute infrastructure using Amazon EC2, Auto Scaling Groups, Load Balancers, and Elastic Block Storage (EBS). Design storage and backup strategies utilizing Amazon S3, EBS snapshots, lifecycle management, and recovery solutions. Implement identity and access management controls using IAM, KMS, Secrets Manager, and security best practices. Develop Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) solutions using Terraform and/or AWS CloudFormation. Establish monitoring, observability, logging, and alerting capabilities using CloudWatch and associated AWS services. Design and implement High Availability (HA) and Disaster Recovery (DR) architectures to meet business continuity objectives. Support infrastructure requirements for Micro Focus or Rocket Enterprise Server hosting environments. Enable secure integration with enterprise systems, databases, middleware, and external platforms. Collaborate with DevOps teams to integrate cloud infrastructure into CI/CD delivery pipelines. Conduct infrastructure sizing, capacity planning, performance tuning, and environment optimization activities. Drive AWS cost optimization initiatives through resource right-sizing, automation, and governance controls. Support migration planning, infrastructure cutovers, validation exercises, and production deployments. Who You Are You’re good at what you do and possess the required experience to prove it. However, equally as important – you have a growth mindset; keen to drive your own personal and professional development. You are customer-focused – someone who prioritizes customer success in their work. And finally, you’re open and borderless – naturally inclusive in how you work with others. Required Technical and Professional Expertise Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or related discipline. 8-12+ years of infrastructure engineering and cloud platform experience. Minimum 5+ years of hands-on AWS architecture, engineering, and environment provisioning experience. Proven experience designing and deploying enterprise-scale AWS environments. Deep understanding of cloud networking, security, infrastructure automation, and operational excellence. Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving skills. Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement abilities. Experience working in complex enterprise transformation or migration programs. Preferred Technical and Professional Experience Experience supporting mainframe modernization and replatforming programs. Experience with Micro Focus Enterprise Server or Rocket Enterprise Server infrastructure deployments. Exposure to enterprise database platforms and cloud-based database architectures. Experience supporting financial services, banking, insurance, or other highly regulated industries. Knowledge of DevSecOps and cloud security frameworks. Experience with infrastructure compliance and governance standards. Being You The “Kyn” in Kyndryl means kinship, which represents the strong bonds we have with each other, our customers and our communities. We focus on ensuring all Kyndryls feel included and we welcome people of all cultures, backgrounds, and experiences. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. We believe in growth, and we’re excited to see what you can bring. At Kyndryl, employee feedback has told us that our number one driver of employee engagement is belonging. That sense of belonging — being a valued, respected, trusted member of the team — is fundamental to our culture and fueling great experiences for our customers. This dedication to welcoming everyone into our company means that Kyndryl gives you the ability to thrive and contribute to our culture of empathy and shared success. That’s The Kyndryl Way. What You Can Expect Your career with us isn’t just a job—it’s an adventure with purpose. We offer a dynamic, hybrid-friendly culture that supports your well-being and empowers you to grow. Our Be Well programs are thoughtfully designed to support your financial, mental, physical, and social health—because we know that when you feel your best, you do your best. From your very first day, you’ll dive into impactful work that powers the systems our customers rely on every day. You won’t just contribute—you’ll make a difference, tackling meaningful projects that sharpen your skills and fuel your growth. We’re here to champion your journey. With powerful tools to chart your career path, personalized development goals aligned with your ambitions, and continuous feedback to keep you inspired and on track, you’ll have everything you need to thrive and evolve. You’ll develop in-demand skills to grow your career and achieve your ambitions with access to cutting-edge learning opportunities—from certifications with Microsoft, Google, and Amazon to coaching and hands-on experiences. And through it all, you’ll be part of a culture that values empathy, restless learning, and a devotion to shared success. We want you to thrive here—and we’re committed to helping you do just that. Ready to make an impact? Join us and help shape what’s next. Get Referred! The role connects physical equipment, gateway runtimes, device connectivity, cloud platforms, digital applications, enterprise identity, and AI-enabled capabilities into a coherent, evolvable architecture. The architect will establish architecture-first delivery practices in which business capabilities, quality attributes, system boundaries, contracts, security requirements, and operational models are defined before implementation. You will translate complex technical decisions into clear recommendations for engineering and business stakeholders, connecting choices to customer value, cost, risk, reliability, delivery timelines, and operational readiness. What you will do Own target architectures, system boundaries, contracts, quality requirements, and technical roadmaps. Document alternatives, assumptions, failure modes, and trade-offs before implementation. Design multi-region routing, tenant and workload isolation, data placement, replication, failover and failback. Define RTO, RPO, availability objectives, and recovery validation for each workload. Enable repeatable regional expansion through reusable infrastructure, automated onboarding, configuration-driven deployment, and application designs that avoid regional forks. Govern industrial edge connectivity, device provisioning, certificate lifecycle, offline behavior, secure OTA updates, and command handling with embedded and safety specialists. Architect cloud services, APIs, real-time integrations, messaging, and data platforms with explicit ownership, compatibility, tenant isolation, and failure behavior. Embed security, observability, capacity planning, cost management, upgrade paths, and operational readiness into every architecture. Establish practical architecture standards, ADRs, reusable platform capabilities, repository boundaries, infrastructure as code, and automated delivery checks. Communicate through clear diagrams, business-focused narratives, and decision options. Lead cross-team reviews, mentor engineers, and build trust with stakeholders. Evaluate AI-assisted engineering and AI-enabled applications with specialist teams, considering business value, privacy, permissions, security, limitations, evaluation, and human oversight. PKI, device identity, and cryptographic architecture Architecture focus: PKI is a foundational device trust system, not merely a subtopic within general identity and security. The role must govern identity from factory provisioning through operational use, renewal, revocation, retirement, and long-lived hardware replacement. Define hardware-backed device identity using IEEE 802.1AR concepts, including factory identity and operational identity, with TPM 2.0 or secure-element roots of trust. Design zero-touch enrollment and renewal using appropriate protocols such as EST, SCEP, or CMPv2, with explicit bootstrap, recovery, renewal, revocation, and offline behavior. Author X.509 certificate profiles aligned with RFC 5280, including subject naming, SAN conventions, EKU constraints, key usage, validity periods, policy OIDs, CRL distribution points, and validation rules. Design CA hierarchies, trust domains, signing boundaries, key ceremonies, offline root protection, intermediate CA operations, HSM integration, and delegated issuance. Govern certificate rotation at fleet scale, including clock drift, intermittent connectivity, dual-certificate overlap, compromised-device recovery, factory reset, ownership transfer, and end-of-life handling. Define cryptographic agility and long-term migration strategies for algorithm changes, including assessment of post-quantum standards such as ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA where appropriate. Standards, RFCs, and normative specifications Establish a reference architecture and standards catalogue that distinguishes mandatory requirements from recommendations. Use RFC 2119 and RFC 8174 terminology consistently when writing normative specifications. Use MUST and MUST NOT for binding requirements; use SHOULD and SHOULD NOT for strong recommendations with documented exceptions; use MAY for permitted options. Maintain versioned specifications for identity, certificate profiles, TLS, MQTT topics, API contracts, event schemas, command semantics, error handling, and regional deployment. Reference applicable standards such as RFC 5280 for X.509 certificates, RFC 7030 for EST, RFC 8446 for TLS 1.3, RFC 6455 for WebSockets, OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect specifications, OpenAPI, and the OASIS MQTT specification. Use ADRs to record context, decision, alternatives, consequences, security impact, operational impact, and conditions for revisiting the decision. Keep C4, deployment, sequence, threat, and data-flow models versioned with the systems they describe. Required experience 14+ years in software engineering, distributed systems, cloud platforms, or systems architecture, including 6+ years leading architecture for complex enterprise, industrial, or mission-critical systems. Proven production delivery and operational experience with multi-region systems, disaster recovery, incident response, and recovery validation. Strong system design judgment and hands-on ability to validate decisions through prototypes, code reviews, performance testing, load testing, and operational evidence. Demonstrated ability to influence multiple teams and explain technical trade-offs to engineering, product, leadership, and non-technical stakeholders. Experience creating standards and governance that enable delivery rather than introducing unnecessary process. Preferred experience Industrial equipment, fleet management, OT cybersecurity, predictive maintenance, digital twins, or large-scale multi-tenant platforms. Platform engineering, technology modernization, and practical exposure to AI-assisted development or enterprise AI integration. Experience with long-lived devices, constrained connectivity, safety-related command paths, and supplier or partner integration. Certifications Certifications are desirable but not mandatory.
